title: A Visit to the Doctor
bigQuestion: How do helpers at the doctor's office keep us well?

story.title: Maya Hears Her Heart
story.kicker: Maya feels nervous at her checkup, until the nurse shares a special tool.
paragraphs: Maya sat on the paper-covered bed. The paper crinkled when she moved. Her tummy felt tight. She squeezed her dad's hand hard.
A nurse named Mr. Ruiz came in with a smile. He said, "It is okay to feel nervous. You can ask me anything." Maya asked, "What is that thing on your neck?"
"This is a stethoscope," said Mr. Ruiz. "It helps me hear your heart." He put the soft ends in Maya's ears. He held the round part on her chest.
Thump-thump. Thump-thump. Maya's eyes got big. "That is my heart!" she said. Her tummy did not feel so tight anymore.
story.think: What helped Maya feel less nervous at her checkup?

lessons.title: Doctors and Nurses
lessons.mainIdea: Doctors and nurses help us stay well and help us get better when we are sick.
reading: Think of a clinic near your home. A *doctor* works there. A doctor checks your body. A doctor helps you get better when you are sick.
A *nurse* works there too. Nurses check how you are doing. They give shots. They answer questions. Doctors and nurses work as a team.

words.d: a person who studied a long time to help keep bodies well
a helper who cares for sick people and checks how they are

look.title: A Busy Clinic
look.text: Picture a clinic. A nurse writes down a boy's height. A doctor looks in a girl's ears. A baby waits on her mom's lap.
look.prompt: Who is working as a team in this clinic?

check.q: Who helps you get better when you are sick?
check.why: A doctor checks your body and helps you get better.

check.q: What is one thing a nurse does?
check.why: The reading says nurses give shots and answer questions.

check.q: How do doctors and nurses work?
check.why: The reading says doctors and nurses work as a team.

lessons.title: Dentists and Pharmacists
lessons.mainIdea: Dentists care for teeth, and pharmacists give out medicine safely.
reading: A *dentist* looks at your teeth. The dentist counts them. The dentist cleans them. The dentist shows you how to brush well.
A *pharmacist* works in a drugstore. A pharmacist gets medicine ready. A pharmacist tells your family how to use it safely.

words.d: a doctor who cares for teeth and gums
a person who gets medicine ready and explains how to use it safely

look.title: Two Helpers
look.text: Look at two pictures. In one, a girl opens her mouth wide in a big chair. In the other, a man in a white coat hands a small bag across a counter.
look.prompt: Which picture shows a dentist? Which shows a pharmacist?

check.q: Who cares for your teeth?
check.why: A dentist is a doctor for teeth and gums.

check.q: Where does a pharmacist work?
check.why: The reading says a pharmacist works in a drugstore.

check.q: What does a pharmacist tell your family?
check.why: A pharmacist explains how to use medicine safely.

lessons.title: Growing Taller
lessons.mainIdea: At a checkup, a nurse measures how tall you are and how much you weigh.
reading: A *checkup* is a visit when you are not sick. It helps you stay well. First, you stand tall against a wall. The nurse measures your height.
Next, you step on a scale. It shows your weight. The doctor looks at these numbers each year. They show that you are growing.

words.d: a visit to the doctor to make sure you are well

look.title: Marks on the Wall
look.text: Look at a door frame at Sam's house. There is a pencil mark for age 4. A higher mark says age 5. The highest mark says age 6.
look.prompt: What do the marks tell you about Sam?

check.q: When do you have a checkup?
choices: Only when you are very sick
When you are well, to stay well
check.why: A checkup is a visit when you are not sick.

check.q: What does a scale show?
check.why: You step on a scale and it shows your weight.

check.q: Why does the doctor look at your height each year?
choices: To see that you are growing
check.why: The numbers show that you are growing.

lessons.title: Heart and Ears
lessons.mainIdea: The doctor uses tools to listen to your heart and look in your ears.
reading: The doctor uses a *stethoscope*. It has two ends for the ears and a round part. The round part goes on your chest. The doctor hears your heart beat.
Then the doctor uses a small light. It helps the doctor look inside your ears. Nothing goes in far. It does not hurt.

words.d: a tool doctors use to listen to your heart and lungs

look.title: Thump-Thump
look.text: Put your hand flat on your chest. Sit very still. Can you feel a soft thump-thump? That is your heart working.
look.prompt: What tool would help you hear your heart even better?

check.q: What does a stethoscope help the doctor do?
check.why: A stethoscope lets the doctor hear your heart beat.

check.q: Where does the round part of the stethoscope go?
check.why: The reading says the round part goes on your chest.

check.q: What does the doctor use to look in your ears?
check.why: The doctor uses a small light to look inside your ears.

lessons.title: Shots Help Us
lessons.mainIdea: Shots help your body learn to fight some germs.
reading: Sometimes you get a shot at a checkup. Many shots are *vaccines*. A vaccine helps your body learn to fight a germ.
A shot can pinch for a moment. You can hold a hand. You can take a big breath. Soon the pinch is gone, and your body is ready.

words.d: a shot or medicine that helps your body learn to fight a germ

look.title: Ready for a Shot
look.text: Picture Leo in the chair. His mom holds his hand. He looks at a poster of a fish. He breathes in slow and breathes out slow.
look.prompt: What things help Leo feel calm?

check.q: What does a vaccine do?
choices: Helps your body learn to fight a germ
check.why: A vaccine helps your body learn to fight a germ.

check.q: How long does a shot pinch?
check.why: The reading says a shot can pinch for a moment.

check.q: What can help you during a shot?
check.why: Holding a hand and big breaths can help.

lessons.title: Asking Questions
lessons.mainIdea: It is okay to feel nervous and to ask questions at the doctor.
reading: Many kids feel *nervous* at the doctor. Adults do too. That is okay. Feelings are part of being a person.
You can ask questions. You can say, "What is that?" or "Will it hurt?" Doctors and nurses like questions. Answers help you feel brave.

words.d: a worried feeling about something that is coming

look.title: Good Questions
look.text: Here are some questions kids ask. What is that tool? What will you do next? Will it hurt? Why do I need this?
look.prompt: What question would you like to ask a doctor?

check.q: Is it okay to feel nervous at the doctor?
check.why: The reading says many kids and adults feel nervous, and that is okay.

check.q: How do doctors feel about questions?
check.why: Doctors and nurses like questions.

check.q: What helps you feel brave?
check.why: The reading says answers help you feel brave.

lessons.title: Medicine From a Trusted Adult
lessons.mainIdea: Take medicine only when a trusted adult gives it to you.
reading: Medicine can help a sick body. But too much can hurt. Some pills look like candy. They are not candy.
Only take *medicine* from a trusted adult. That could be a parent, a grown-up at home or the school nurse. If you find pills, do not touch them. Tell an adult.

words.d: something that helps a sick body get better when used the right way
a grown-up who keeps you safe, like a parent or school nurse

look.title: Pills on the Floor
look.text: Ana sees small pink pills on the kitchen floor. They look like candy. Her grandpa is in the next room.

check.q: Who should give you medicine?
check.why: Only take medicine from a trusted adult.

check.q: What should you do if you find pills?
choices: Do not touch them and tell an adult
check.why: The reading says do not touch them and tell an adult.

check.q: Why is medicine not candy?
check.why: Medicine can help, but too much can hurt.

lessons.title: Calling 911
lessons.mainIdea: In an emergency, call 911 to get help fast.
reading: An *emergency* is when someone is badly hurt or in danger. It needs help right away. A fire is an emergency. A person who will not wake up is an emergency.
Call *911* on a phone. Stay calm. Say what is wrong. Say where you are. Stay on the phone until the helper says you can hang up.

words.d: a time when someone needs help right away
the phone number to call for fast help in an emergency

look.title: What to Say
look.text: The helper on the phone asks: What is wrong? Where are you? You answer: My grandma fell and will not wake up. We are at 12 Oak Street.
look.prompt: What two things did you tell the helper?

check.q: What number do you call in an emergency?
check.why: 911 is the number for fast help.

check.q: Which one is an emergency?
check.why: A fire needs help right away.

check.q: When can you hang up?
choices: When the helper says you can
check.why: Stay on the phone until the helper says you can hang up.

review.q: Who helps you take care of your teeth?
review.why: A dentist is a doctor for teeth and gums.

review.q: What tool lets you hear a heart?
review.why: A stethoscope lets you hear the heart beat.

choices: A visit to make sure you are well
review.why: A checkup is a visit when you are not sick.

review.q: In the story, what helped Maya feel better?
review.why: The nurse let Maya hear her heart, and her tummy felt less tight.
Only take medicine from a trusted adult.

review.q: What do you say when you call 911?
choices: What is wrong and where you are
review.why: Tell the helper what is wrong and where you are.
